Glasstual

Privacy

Glasstual is an IRC client. It has no Glasstual account, no advertising, no analytics and no automatic update check. It connects to the networks and peers you choose and keeps its settings and chat history on your Mac.

Data on Your Mac

Glasstual stores server settings, preferences and the certificates you have trusted for encrypted file transfers in its own container on your Mac. It also keeps conversation history there, so it can restore conversations between sessions and search them. Transcript log files are written only if you turn logging on, to the folder you choose.

Server, account, proxy and channel passwords, OAuth tokens, SASL signing keys and the certificate Glasstual creates for encrypted file transfers are stored in the macOS Keychain. Commands you configure to run when connecting may contain sensitive text and stay in local settings. Files you receive are saved in Downloads or a folder you select, and are marked as downloaded from the internet.

An exported settings file never includes Keychain passwords or certificate references, and includes connect commands only if you choose to.

You can clear a conversation’s scrollback in the app. Turning off transcript logging stops new log files from being written; it does not delete files already saved. Removing the app may leave its local data and Keychain items on your Mac. Contact support if you need help removing them.

Spotlight, Shortcuts and Focus

By default Glasstual adds the names of your servers and channels, with the server name as a keyword, to the system Spotlight index on your Mac. Names of direct conversations are added only if you turn that setting on. Message text is never added. Turning the settings off removes the items Glasstual indexed.

Shortcuts actions run on your Mac and act on the servers and conversations you choose; sending a message asks you to confirm it first. A Focus filter only changes how Glasstual notifies you and whether it sets you away while that Focus is active.

IRC Connections

When you connect to an IRC network, Glasstual sends the connection details, nickname, authentication information and messages needed to use that network. The network and other participants may see or retain what you send according to their own practices. Glasstual does not operate those networks.

Some information is sent only on servers that support it:

  • If you register an account, the account name, password and any email address you enter are sent to that network.
  • If you set a profile, its display name, picture address and color are stored by the server and shown to other people.
  • Typing notifications and the position you have read up to are shared by default. You can turn each off in IRCv3 settings.
  • Glasstual answers client-to-client (CTCP) requests such as VERSION by default. You can turn this off in Connection settings.

If the server’s certificate was not checked, Glasstual asks before it sends your account password. If a connection that should be encrypted is not, the password is not sent.

WebSocket and Proxies

A server set to WebSocket carries the same IRC data through the network’s WebSocket gateway. With “Connect securely” on, the connection is encrypted (wss://); without it, it is not (ws://).

A server set to use a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy, or Tor, connects through it, so the IRC network sees the proxy’s address instead of yours. The proxy’s operator can see that you connect and where. Tor connections go through Tor Browser, which must be running. Choosing Connect Without Proxy connects directly that one time.

File Transfers and Direct Chats

File transfers and direct chats (DCC) connect your Mac straight to the other participant’s computer, not through the IRC server and not through a server’s proxy. That participant sees your IP address. They are unencrypted unless you use the secure options, which encrypt the connection with TLS and identify each side by a certificate you choose whether to trust.

To tell the other side where to connect, Glasstual asks your router for your public address. If the router does not provide it, Glasstual contacts api.ipify.org by default. A setting can instead use one of wtfismyip.com, canhazip.com or ifconfig.me, or avoid these lookups by using a router-only or manual address.

Links and Images

Inline images are off by default. If you turn them on, Glasstual fetches images linked in messages over HTTP or HTTPS, with limits on size. The image host receives the request and can see your IP address. Each channel can turn them off separately. Glasstual does not fetch link previews.

Profile pictures that people set on a network are fetched the same way, only when both inline images and server profiles are turned on. If a network advertises its own icon, Glasstual fetches it for the sidebar whether or not inline images are on.

Images never go around a server’s proxy:

  • With Tor, images, profile pictures and network icons load through Tor.
  • With a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy, an image linked in a message loads through the proxy only when you click it. Profile pictures and network icons are not loaded.
  • If the proxy has no address, nothing is loaded.

Before a link opens in your browser or another app, Glasstual asks. The app’s privacy settings and the destination site’s policy then apply.

This Website

This site is hosted on GitHub Pages and uses no cookies or analytics. The home page asks GitHub’s API for the latest release so the download button can link to it. Both requests are subject to GitHub’s privacy statement.

Support and Your Choices

If you email us or open a GitHub issue, we receive the information you choose to provide. Please do not include passwords, private messages or unredacted logs in a report. Support correspondence remains in our mailbox or issue history until it is deleted. You can ask us to delete our copy by emailing hello@vakesz.com. Public GitHub issues are also subject to GitHub’s privacy statement.

Questions about this policy can be sent to hello@vakesz.com.
